name: Snow Leopard's Tears Waterfall
full: Snow Leopard's Tears Waterfall (Bars Tears; Barskoon Gorge)
near: Barskoon village (Barskaun) at the gorge entrance — about 15–17 km along the gorge road to the parking area by the waterfalls (Nomad's Land, Silk Road Adventures). Karakol — about 90 km.
elev: About 2,470 m above sea level (Silk Road Adventures; the waterfall cascade — 2,470–2,700 m). Nomad's Land gives 2,300 m for the waterfall area.
short: The best-known waterfall of the cascade in Barskoon Gorge — a natural monument, 30–40 minutes on foot from the Kumtor road.
desc: Snow Leopard's Tears is the main and most accessible waterfall of the Barskoon Gorge cascade on the southern shore of Issyk-Kul (together with “Champagne Spray”, “Manas's Bowl” and “Aksakal's Beard”). The water falls in several steps in a narrow canyon among Tian Shan spruces; at the foot the noise is so loud that no other sounds can be heard, and the spray flies dozens of metres. The height differs between sources: about 100 m according to Trip to Kyrgyzstan and 2GIS (probably the whole cascade), about 20 m for the main step according to Silk Road Adventures. The waterfall has the status of a state natural monument; in winter it freezes into an ice “palace” under which water continues to flow. According to legend, the waterfall is the tears of a female snow leopard mourning her cubs who died on the rocks.
guide: Leave your car by the Kumtor road near the yurt cafés and follow the trail up for 1.6 km — in 30–35 minutes you're at Snow Leopard's Tears. If you have energy left, 20 minutes higher up is “Champagne Spray”, and another hour on, with 300–350 m of gain, is “Manas's Bowl”: allow 3–4 hours for all three. The trail is not marked and is slippery from the spray — don't go up to the stream itself; good shots come from a distance. On the way into the gorge, stop at the monument to Yuri Gagarin (the cosmonaut only drove through here, but the legend lives on). In winter come for the ice sculptures — the waterfall freezes completely.
see: The Snow Leopard's Tears waterfall itself with its stepped cascades in a spruce canyon; higher up — “Champagne Spray” (~2,500 m, 20 min) and “Manas's Bowl” (~2,700 m, another 1 h); from the road you can see the “Rocky” waterfall; monuments to Yuri Gagarin and a Vostok capsule in the gorge; yurts with kumys by the parking area; in winter — ice cascades.
skip: You find it hard to walk 30–40 minutes uphill on a slippery, rocky, unmarked trail. You've already seen large waterfalls (Abshir-Ata, Arslanbob) and aren't ready to spend a day on the road from Cholpon-Ata/Bishkek. You're going right after heavy rain — the trail is especially dangerous.
diff: Easy to medium: 1.6 km one way, 30–35 min of climbing to Snow Leopard's Tears; the trail is unmarked, slippery and rocky. The lower cascade is accessible to children (DWC); to Manas's Bowl it is already medium (+300–350 m).
when: June–September: full water and the yurt cafés are open; late May — early June — peak snowmelt. In winter (December–February) the waterfall freezes — beautiful ice formations, but the trail becomes icy; the Kumtor road is cleared year-round.
hours: Open natural area, open 24 hours; no ticket offices or time restrictions. The yurt cafés by the parking area — summer only. Daylight lasts until 17:00: after that it is hard to catch a marshrutka (minibus)/taxi back (Nomad's Land).
daytime: Until noon — early afternoon: fewer people, the sun lights the gorge; return to the highway before 17:00. In the heat it is cool at the waterfall from the spray.
how: Along the southern-shore highway to the village of Barskoon (Bishkek — Barskoon about 315 km, 5–5.5 h; Karakol — Barskoon ~90 km, ~1.5 h). In the village turn south into the gorge along a good dirt road to Kumtor/Arabel; after ~15–17 km there is a parking area by the yurts and the start of the trail, then 1.6 km on foot.
needcar: Yes, to the parking area it is 15–17 km along the gorge from the village: your own car (almost any car can make it — Too.kg), a taxi or a tour. On foot from the village — a whole day.
self: Yes: no fee or permits needed, the trail is short. You need transport to the parking area and an offline map; the trail has no signs — keep to the main stream bed.
roadtype: Paved road along the southern-shore highway; in the gorge — a well-worn dirt road to Kumtor (“a good dirt road to Arabel”, almost any car and motorcycle can pass — Too.kg). The last 1.6 km is a rocky footpath.
traveltime: From Karakol ~1.5–2 h one way (MYWAY: 4 h round trip, 200 km); from Bishkek 5–5.5 h; from Cholpon-Ata ~3.5 h. On foot from the parking area to Snow Leopard's Tears 30–35 min; all three waterfalls — 3–4 h.
stay: Tent — there are many places to pitch one in the gorge (Too.kg). In Barskoon village and neighbouring Tamga — guesthouses and yurt camps of the southern shore: budget from 500–600 som/person (economist.kg, July 2026). Trip to Kyrgyzstan mentions yurt camps nearby (specific names and 2025–2026 prices not confirmed).
net: Coverage in the gorge is partial (Too.kg). In Barskoon village and on the highway — Beeline/O!/MegaCom. Don't count on a signal at the waterfall itself.
entry: Free: no source (too.kg, Nomad's Land, mir24, DWC, 2023–2026) reports an entrance fee/eco fee in Barskoon Gorge.
transfer: Taxi Karakol — waterfalls 3,500 som per car one way (Nomad's Land); MYWAY Karakol — Barskoon — Karakol 9,900 som per car for up to 5 people (2025–2026); Tripster from Karakol €250 per group of 1–7 people; marshrutka Karakol — Barskoon ~100 som (another 15–17 km to the parking area).
bring: Trekking shoes with a tread (slippery), a windbreaker/rain jacket against the spray, water and a snack, cash for the yurt café (kumys), in winter — crampons/ice cleats. Don't drink water from the Barskoon River: Kumtor is upstream (Too.kg); drink from springs.
warn: The trail is unmarked, wet and slippery; don't go close to the stream — a safe distance is about 100 m (mir24). In winter — ice on the trail. Don't drink water from the main river below Kumtor. Heavy Kumtor trucks run on the road — be careful on the dirt road. The names of the cascade's waterfalls are confused in different sources — check against the map (2GIS).
food: Kumys and tea in the summer yurt cafés by the parking area (Too.kg, Nomad's Land); in Barskoon and on the highway — lagman, beshbarmak, smoked Issyk-Kul fish.
reviews: 2GIS: 5/5, 106 ratings (viewed 07.10.2026). Google Maps: a separate listing could not be matched (meta). Tripster excursion “Skazka and Barskaun”: 4.84, 108 ratings. Pros: a spectacular cascade in a spruce gorge, a short trail, yurts with kumys, ice formations in winter. Cons: a slippery unmarked trail, confusion over waterfall names, the long road from Bishkek.
p.sum: The easiest way is from Karakol (≈90 km) or from the southern shore: along the highway to Barskoon, then 15–20 km along the good Kumtor dirt road (almost any car can make it) to the parking area with yurt cafés and 30–35 min on foot (1.6 km) along a slippery trail. Without a car — a marshrutka to Barskoon (~100 som from Karakol) and a taxi into the gorge, or a taxi from Karakol (3,500 som one way) / a MYWAY transfer (9,900 som per car round trip). Entry is free, overnight stays are in guesthouses in Barskoon and Tamga ($22–36) or in a tent in the gorge.
